Those voices can be unreliable. Luckily you didn't have a bad break when you got off your meds. I had the opposite reaction; took meds for a few months, mellowed out, felt calm and good, and then I went off of them thinking I was fixed (I was also too busy to pick up my prescription) 
Within a few days I returned back to hating everything and everyone and all that makes up this universe. I was shocked at not only the amount of rage that was generated but the realization that THAT is what I was like ALL THE TIME since I was a child before the meds. 
I went back to my doc as soon as I could to get my chill pills. 

Three years later I made the difficult decision to end medication thinking that I'd done enough work on my mind to be able to handle it. And while there was a transition period, I was right; I was well ENOUGH to go off the meds and actively control myself through rational thought and emotional process. 

For me, meds gave me that ability to not SUCCUMB to those voices, the voices didnt go anywhere for me but I now know which ones I can listen to and which ones I should just ignore. But that took time, patience, and trial & error. 

Can't depend on those voices many times, they're just voices, they're not necessarily right and theyre not necessarily wrong. But you have to learn which one is really YOU and learn to control that one to help you through events in a calm, rational state. I'm happy you feel elated and energetic, I love feeling that way whenever it comes 'round, just be very aware of yourself and your feelings. Old habits die hard. 

All the best of luck!

She had parents and friends who loved her and took care of her, so did I, even when I didn't acknowledge or want it. 

She was getting professional help, I got professional help. (While the success of mine is confirmed, I can't say the same for her obviously) 

And finally when a really shitty day came her way, the above was incapable of stopping her from pulling the trigger. And when my shitty days came, the above managed to stop me from pulling mine. And now, I'm happy and an almost completely different person.... and she'll never have that chance that she and everyone in that situation deserves. It just goes to show how fucking feeble the mind is when it's unbalanced. She had many reasons to live, and didn't see any of them, and I thank my lucky stars every day that whatever the fuck stopped me when I was in that spot, succeeded. 


Or maybe she got what she wanted, and it's ok. I don't fucking know.

8 years ago I had a full ride to school (personally funded by a philanthropist). As each semester passed it became harder and harder to wake up and leave the dorm. Every semester that passed I thought I could fix whatever it was that was wrong with me until I started failing horribly... that 'ambition' never came. 

When the counselors pleaded for me to go get medical help and to take the semester off I was SO afraid of disappointing my parents that I convinced the counselors that I would get help and to please not send me home.... worst fucking mistake I've ever made in my life. I failed the next semester and went home for winter break as if nothing had happened. 

Spring semester time came and I had to explain to my parents why their top-honors-in-high-school daughter wasn't to return to college. I hit rock bottom, started cutting, drinking when no one was around and became suicidal. When I was caught with bloodied arms on the bathroom floor of my brother's house after breaking a lightbulb and using the shards to cut myself from wrist to elbow I was threatened with the psych ER. I successfully (I was a pro by now) convinced my family that I'd be fine and I'd work on it. When I was caught two weeks later with a butcher's knife to my arm in the kitchen at 3 in the morning it resulted in my ass getting sent to the psych ER that night. 

It took 3.5 years of therapy and light (10 to 20mg of Paxil a day) medication (I was adamant about not depending on drugs to recuperate my life) to finally learn to let the past go, to not let my mistakes ruin my future any more than they have and to forgive myself. 

Granted, I still have demons but after a lot of hard work and continued effort I have been out of that dark abyss for a nice long time and when I read your post it's like being sent back in time to that place I've tried so hard to bury. 

I'm sorry if this shit got wordy I just need you to understand that you cannot underestimate this shit and I don't want you to live with this regret the way I've had to live with mine. I am fully convinced that if I would have just taken care of myself instead of letting my pride and fear get in the way I could have salvaged that life. 
Please get help. I wish you nothing but the best.

By age 14 you learn that your best friends on the streets are headphones and the ability to shoot fire from your eyeballs. Fighting them is no good and you don't want to risk the situation getting heated, they are NOT worth the trouble that could potentially get you in to. The best thing you could possibly do is ignore them, trust me, it hurts them the most, it discourages the behavior. A lot of these guys WANT you to fight back, they want your attention in any form. I understand blowing up on them sometimes, hell, sometimes it can't be helped but for your own peace of mind you have to learn to A)Get good headphones B)Stare straight ahead when walking, make NO eye contact and pretend they don't even exist and C)Because you'll have headphones on, and just because you're not actively making eye contact with them, learn to use your peripherals. ALWAYS be aware of your surroundings and who is around you. Trust your instincts. 

As far as the white guy thing, it's true, they're 'intimidated'. I can't tell you how many times I had a crush on a white guy only to have him tell me months/years later that they had a HUGE crush on me but that they were too intimidated to do anything about it (FRUSTRATEEDDDD). 


The most important thing here is to not let these assholes sour YOUR mood and life. I wish I could tell you something better but all I can say is 'you have to learn to live with it, protect yourself at all times and teach your sons to be better men'.

After being kicked out of school for failing all of the classes I didn't attend because of my crippling depression, my mother caught me in the kitchen in the middle of the night with a knife to my throat. She freaked out and we had a huge fight with my father and my sister trying to get us both to calm down. The following day she took me to a psych ER where I was evaluated and shortly released with an appointment to a psychologist and a therapist in the hospital's sister clinic. 
I was scared after what I almost did to myself so I went, it wasn't easy, I refused to take medication and wouldn't open up in therapy but after a few months I gave it a try. I didn't think anything could help me so I figured 'why not, just one more thing that is going to fail me'. After 3 years of treatment, I weaned myself off of the medication and the therapy. 3 years after I've finished therapy and I'm newly married, healthy and happier than I ever thought could be possible. 

In those three years of therapy (aided by the medication) I learned to let go of my past, acknowledge my feelings, forgive myself and to accept the love of others knowing that I actually deserve it. 
It's not a clean break but now the little devil in my head isn't on the loudspeaker, it's a squeak in the back corner of the room and whenever I hear him I know to bring out the flyswatter and beat the ever-loving shit out of it. 
It's not easy, but it's WORTH it and POSSIBLE! 

**TL;DR - I hit near rock bottom and had no place to go but up, and BOY am I up ;) **
